answer: Every new agent must land on a narrow jetty: admission needs sponsors from several disjoint invite-tree branches with no shared ancestor above a set depth, and each sponsor's weight is divided by the admissions its branch has carried. Dilution makes branch influence ripple outward and fade with every clone landed. A farm cloning through one inlet exhausts its branch weight fast; remaining sponsors must be genuine independent identities it cannot manufacture. Scarcity and dilution make each additional clone costlier than the last, so voting power tracks cross-branch diversity, not head count.
